book.title: Femoroacetabular Impingement Syndrome and Labral Presentations

blocks.text: The hip is a ball-and-socket joint. The ball is the femoral head and the socket is the acetabulum. A rim of soft cartilage, the **labrum**, deepens the socket and helps seal the joint. **Femoroacetabular impingement (FAI)** means that the shape of the ball, the socket, or both causes early contact between them at the end of some hip movements, especially deep flexion with inward rotation [Ref - to verify]. Two main shapes are described:

rows: The ball is not fully round and has an extra bump at the head-neck junction
The socket covers too much of the ball, or is deeper or tilted

blocks.text: These shape differences are common in people without pain, including athletes [Ref - to verify]. For this reason, an international consensus describes **FAI syndrome** as a clinical diagnosis that needs all three of these: a typical pattern of motion-related or position-related hip pain, clinical signs, and imaging findings of a cam or pincer shape [Ref - to verify exact statement]. A shape on imaging alone is not FAI syndrome.

Labral tears often occur with FAI, but a labral tear is also seen in people without pain. FAI syndrome affects young and middle-aged active adults, and some people develop hip osteoarthritis later, although the link is not fully understood [Ref - to verify].

items: Pain in the groin, sometimes the outer hip or buttock, brought on by deep flexion, twisting, sitting for a long time, getting out of a car, squatting, or pivoting sports.
A sharp catch, click or pain with certain movements, and sometimes locking or giving way.
Stiffness and reduced flexion or internal rotation.
The C sign: the patient cups the hand over the side of the hip with the thumb behind the trochanter and fingers in the groin when describing the pain. It is a pointer, not a diagnosis.
Often aged 20 to 50 and active.

rows: Where is the pain, and can you show me with your hand?
Groin or front hip supports an intra-articular source
What movements or positions trigger it: deep squat, twisting, sitting low, getting out of the car?
Do you feel catching, clicking or locking?
Any past childhood hip disease, injury or surgery?
Any back or buttock pain with leg symptoms?
Is it bilateral, and how does your sport or work load the hip?
Any night pain, fever, weight loss?
Any groin bulge or pain with coughing?
For adolescents: any limp and recent growth?

blocks.text: Honest note: no clinical test confirms FAI or a labral tear. Most hip impingement tests are sensitive but not specific, so a negative result lowers the chance of an intra-articular problem more than a positive result proves a diagnosis [Ref - to verify]. Use the findings together with the history and imaging.
E1. FADIR (flexion, adduction, internal rotation) impingement test

rows: Move the hip into a position where a cam or pincer shape and the labrum are most likely to be loaded
Beside the hip; one hand on the knee and the other on the ankle or foot
Flex the hip to about 90 degrees, then adduct and internally rotate it by moving the foot outward; stop at the first pain or at end range
Reproduction of the familiar groin or hip pain, sometimes with a block to movement or a click
A positive test supports an intra-articular hip problem such as FAI, labral injury or OA
Low specificity; a negative result makes an intra-articular problem less likely but does not exclude it [Ref - to verify]
Moving too fast; forcing end range; counting a stretch feeling or buttock pain as positive
Check range, other tests and imaging need

blocks.text: E2. FABER (Patrick) test

See Vol 7 Ch 1. Groin pain suggests a hip joint source and posterior pelvic pain suggests a sacroiliac source. The distance of the knee from the bed may be compared with the other side as a measure of range.
E3. Hip range of movement

rows: Measure passive hip flexion and internal rotation with a goniometer or inclinometer, and compare with the other side
Reduced flexion or internal rotation, especially with pain at the end of range, supports FAI-type restriction
Normal values differ between people, and range may be reduced because of pain or muscle guarding [Ref - to verify]

blocks.text: E4. Log roll test

rows: Check for pain from hip joint structures with minimal muscle loading
Supine with legs straight and relaxed
Roll the whole leg inward and outward by holding the thigh or lower leg
Groin pain or a click; a firm block

blocks.text: E5. Resisted straight leg raise (Stinchfield) test

rows: The patient lifts the straight leg to about 30 degrees against resistance
Hip joint or iliopsoas involvement; not specific

blocks.text: E6. Scour test and other tests
See Vol 7 Ch 1. Catching or locking on movement may suggest a labral tear.
E7. Imaging

X-ray (anteroposterior pelvis and a lateral view) and MRI or MR arthrography are ordered by a doctor to look for a cam or pincer shape, labral tears and cartilage damage. They are not needed for every patient, and they should be interpreted with the clinical findings [Ref - to verify].
E8. Outcome measures
International Hip Outcome Tool (iHOT-12 or iHOT-33) and the Hip disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (HOOS) [Ref - to verify].

rows: Older, stiff, reduced internal rotation, X-ray changes
Lateral hip pain, trochanter tenderness, single-leg stance pain
Pain with palpation of the tendon, squeeze test, cough, abdominal wall
Slipped capital femoral epiphysis or Perthes in the young
Audible or palpable snap with movement

sections.title: G. RED FLAGS AND URGENT CONDITIONS

rows: Adolescent with a limp and limited or painful hip rotation
Pain with impact, runner or low bone density
After a fall: cannot bear weight, shortened externally rotated leg
Constant night pain, weight loss, cancer history
Sudden severe pain with steroid use, alcohol or sickle cell disease
Locked hip with a true mechanical block
Loose body or large labral tear
Saddle numbness, bladder or bowel change

sections.title: H. Working diagnosis and decision pathway

items: Any emergency or urgent flag? **Yes:** act as in Section G.

Motion- or position-related groin or front hip pain, a positive FADIR test and other signs, reduced flexion or internal rotation, and no other cause? **Yes:** working diagnosis is suspected FAI syndrome. Confirmation requires imaging findings of a cam or pincer shape by a doctor.
Catching or locking and positive provocation tests? Suspect a labral tear and arrange medical review if it persists.
Begin education, activity modification and exercise therapy.
If there is no improvement after a good trial or if there is a mechanical block, discuss specialist review, including arthroscopic options [Ref - to verify].

rows: Hip joint mobilization (gentle long-axis distraction or lateral glides)
Short-term pain relief in some patients
Pain increases or a catch develops

blocks.text: **Preferred starting choice:** education, activity modification and exercise therapy. Manual therapy is a minor adjunct. Do not use techniques that force the hip into the impingement position. Avoid repeated end-range flexion and internal rotation stretching. Do not claim that manual therapy reshapes the bone or repairs the labrum.

sections.title: J. Exercise prescription (example starting plan, not universal)

blocks.text: **Principle:** a supervised, progressive program of hip and trunk strengthening, movement control and activity modification is a first-line option. Trials comparing physiotherapy with hip arthroscopy show improvement in both groups, with arthroscopy giving larger gains in pain and function at about 12 months in some trials [Ref - to verify]. The choice depends on the patient's goals, the severity, a sport or work demand and the response to rehabilitation, and is made with the orthopaedic surgeon.

rows: Pain-free range, walking, cycling with a higher seat, relative rest from deep flexion and twisting
Bridge, side-lying abduction, clam, hip hinge, sit-to-stand to a higher chair, trunk stability (dead bug, side plank)
Step-up, split squat, single-leg squat, Romanian deadlift, controlled squat to a pain-free depth
Control, no catch or groin pain
Running progression, change of direction, sport drills

blocks.text: **Activity modification:** avoid deep squats, low seats, sitting with the knees above the hips for long periods, and repeated pivoting under load early on. Shorten stride, add cushioned shoes and adjust bike seat height as needed. Aim to reduce, not remove, activity.
**Symptom rule:** pain up to about 3 to 4 out of 10 that settles within 24 hours is acceptable. Sharp pain, catching or locking means stop and reassess.

**Return to sport criteria (example):** pain-free daily activity, near-normal strength compared with the other side, good single-leg control, and tolerance of sport drills with no catch or groin pain. If surgery is performed, follow the surgeon's protocol, which usually limits range and weight-bearing at first [Ref - to verify].

**Medical options (decided by doctors):** anti-inflammatory medicines, intra-articular injections for pain relief or for diagnostic purposes, and hip arthroscopy for selected patients with FAI syndrome who do not improve with rehabilitation or who have a mechanical block [Ref - to verify].

blocks.text: **Case:** A 28-year-old recreational footballer has 8 months of right groin pain with deep squats, getting out of the car and kicking. He feels an occasional catch. FADIR reproduces his groin pain. Passive hip flexion and internal rotation are reduced compared with the other side. Hip strength is good. Lumbar and neurological findings are normal. No red flags. An X-ray (ordered by his doctor) shows a cam shape.

**Working diagnosis:** FAI syndrome (cam-type) with possible labral involvement. **Plan:** education, activity modification, hip and trunk strengthening, graded return to kicking, reassess in 4 to 6 weeks, and an orthopaedic opinion if he does not improve or develops locking.
**Questions and answers**

items: Why is a cam shape on X-ray not enough to diagnose FAI syndrome? Cam shapes are common in people without pain, so the diagnosis also needs matching symptoms and examination findings.

Why is a negative FADIR test more useful than a positive one? It is sensitive but not specific, so a negative result makes an intra-articular problem less likely, while a positive result can come from many hip problems.
Why avoid stretching into flexion and internal rotation? That is the position where the shapes meet, so stretching there may irritate the joint.
A 14-year-old has knee pain and a limp with painful hip rotation. What do you do? Treat it as urgent and refer for slipped capital femoral epiphysis.

When do you refer for surgery? After a reasonable trial of rehabilitation without improvement, a true mechanical block, or when function goals cannot be met, with the decision made with the surgeon [Ref - to verify].
**Initial approach:** screen flags, then education, activity modification and exercise therapy.
**Justifying findings:** motion-related groin pain, positive FADIR, reduced flexion and internal rotation, imaging shape.
**Priority:** build hip and trunk strength and control, avoid provoking positions early.
**Manual therapy:** minor adjunct.
**Exercise:** bridge, abduction, hinge, functional strength, sport drills.
**Modalities:** limited role.
**Tell the patient:** the shape is common; many people improve with rehabilitation; surgery is an option for some.
**Avoid:** forcing end-range impingement, diagnosing from imaging alone, ignoring adolescent hip signs.
**Measure:** iHOT-12 or HOOS, pain, range, single-leg control.
**If no improvement:** orthopaedic review.
**Referral triggers:** Section G.
**Discharge:** function and sport goals met with a maintenance plan.

blocks.text: **Assumptions:** adult, no urgent flags, no advanced hip osteoarthritis.

items: **Can be tested:** how physiotherapy compares with arthroscopy; which patients do well without surgery.
**Hypotheses:** that avoiding impingement positions and improving control reduces joint stress; that shape changes contribute to later osteoarthritis (uncertain).
**Future questions:** best exercise dose, which shapes are harmful, and long-term outcomes.

blocks.text: Evidence not graded until references are verified.

sections.title: Now You Should Be Able To

items: Explain cam and pincer shapes and why imaging alone does not make a diagnosis.
Perform FADIR and range tests and state their limits.
Recognise adolescent hip emergencies and mechanical blocks.
Build a staged strengthening and return plan.

sections.A: Hip ek ball-and-socket jor hai jis ke kinare par labrum hota hai. FAI mein ball ya socket ki shakal (cam ya pincer) se gehri movement par takkar hoti hai, aur labrum zakhmi ho sakta hai.
sections.B: Groin mein dard, kabhi hip ke bahar ya kooleh mein, gehre jhukne, mudne, der tak baithne ya gaari se utarne par.
sections.C: Dard kahan hai (haath se dikhayein), kaun si positions dard deti hain, aur kya clicking ya atakna hai.
sections.D: Chaal, hip ki range (flexion, rotation) aur taaqat dekhein.
sections.E: Koi test FAI ya labral tear confirm nahi karta. FADIR jaise tests aksar positive aate hain lekin specific nahi; negative test zyada madadgar hai.
sections.F: Hip OA, gluteal tendinopathy, groin strain aur kamar se aata dard isi jaise lag sakte hain.
sections.G: Langrata naujawan aur hip rotation dard wali ya kam (growth plate ka masla), ya runner mein impact se dard (stress fracture): urgent refer.
sections.H: Red flags na hon, movement ya position se groin dard, positive tests aur imaging mein shakal ki tabdeeli: FAI syndrome.
sections.I: Hip flexors, adductors aur gluteals par soft tissue kaam, aur hip mobilisation exercise ko aasaan banane ke liye.
sections.J: Supervised, dheere dheere barhta hip aur trunk strengthening, movement control aur dard wali positions kam karna.
sections.L: Naujawanon mein flags screen karein, FAI ko shakal aur load ka masla samjhayein, 3 mahine exercise, phir zaroorat ho to surgeon.
sections.M: Dard, iHOT-12 ya HOOS, FADIR, hip flexion aur rotation, aur taaqat dobara dekhein.
sections.N: 28 saal ke footballer ko gehre squat aur gaari se utarne par groin dard hai. Khud socho, phir jawab dekho.
